title: Spring Boot .properties import drops keys whose first character is an escaped # or ! (\#general=...)

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue/PR; short error excerpt quoted.

symptom: Keys written with a backslash-escaped leading character, such as '\#general=...', '\#alerts=...' and '\!oncall=...', are missing from the Environment (lookup returns null) when the file is loaded through spring.config.import. Keys that need no escaping load normally, and java.util.Properties reads the same file correctly.
cause: Boot's properties loader (OriginTrackedPropertiesLoader) treats a line as a comment when its first character is an escaped # or !, and drops the whole line. java.util.Properties decides comments from the raw first character before unescaping, so it keeps these keys.
fixSummary: Do not load the file through spring.config.import. Register it with @PropertySource("classpath:routes.properties") on a configuration class, which uses the java.util.Properties based loader, and remove the spring.config.import line. Keep the key names unchanged. Fixed in Boot 4.0.9.
